title: Synthesis of graphitic nanofibres using iron (III) oxide catalyst for hydrogen storage application
material_description: Fe-GNF 9 | graphitic nanofibre, herringbone morphology (TEM), grown by chemical vapour decomposition of C2H4 over unsupported Fe2O3 catalyst (0.05 g in quartz boat) at 600 °C for 4 h with C2H4/H2 flow 30:70 mL min-1 (Taguchi L9 run 9); used as prepared; XRD shows graphite (002) and Fe3C
source_location: main-5.png (p. 224), Fig. 4, Adsorption series (blue diamonds), marker 1 of the visible adsorption markers
notes: archive: HYC-0067_fig4_adsorption.json; marker at the origin partly hidden by the axes, centroid of its visible part; BET area from Table 3 (Quantachrome Autosorb 1, N2; BET samples degassed 4 h at 250 °C); interlayer spacing d002 printed as 3·423 Å (Table 3), stored as 0.3423 nm; residual catalyst: XRD of Fe-GNF 9 shows only Fe3C besides graphite, Fe content not stated; H2 by 'gravimetric measurement', instrument not named, no buoyancy correction stated, basis not named; sample degassed at 250 °C for 12 h before H2, brought to 77 K in liquid nitrogen (77 K printed); wt% convention not defined for Fig. 4 (the Table 1 footnote definition applies to the literature values in Table 1 only); acknowledgement thanks University of Nottingham for 'collaboration studies as well as facilities' but the paper does not say where the H2 measurement was made, so the lab is the corresponding author's
